subject: MAP heat-check: contingency grid & decision ladder
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acmehealth.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: maya.singh@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-06-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Timeline risk: MAP gating concerns and next steps

Priya —

Quick note from our side: after the sync this morning we ran the MAP against our internal evaluation calendar. Two of our technical reviewers have availability slippage (one out for travel, one reprioritized to a SOC2 task). That pushes our internal acceptance window by at least 2 weeks unless we open a parallel review lane.

We need to know: can Redwood commit to one of the following by Friday so we can decide on our side?
- Provide a short, scoped test harness (2-hour runbook + scoring rubric) we can run asynchronously with an engineer review (low-friction)
- Offer a temporary extension of the hosted evaluation instance for an extra 10 days with priority support
- Or accept a firm go/no-go decision ladder so we can present to procurement and legal

I attached the MAP export (acme_map_v2.xlsx) and a quick risk log. We want to avoid shifting the close date if possible — that's painful for internal budgeting.

Will you advise on the best path?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Health

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I read the MAP and the risk log. We can do a hybrid path to avoid a full close slip. Proposal below (quick summary + asks):

Quick proposal (options we can execute this week):
1) Async sandbox + rubric (Preferred immediate step) — Redwood provides a 10-day scoped evaluation sandbox pre-configured with the candidate model and a 2-hour test harness doc. We will supply a triage engineer to review results within 24 hours of submission. Deliverable: acme_async_runbook.md + temporary token + runbook checklist.
2) Priority hosted extension — 10-day extension of evaluation instance with a dedicated support engineer (subject to billing/credits).
3) Decision ladder — if Acme can sign-off on acceptance gates by next Tuesday, we hold the close date and proceed. If not, we accept a two-week re-baseline and create an escrow of dev time to preserve price/terms for 30 days.

Immediate asks for option 1 to be actionable:
- Can you share the two test cases your reviewers will not be able to hit? I want to keep the async harness focused and avoid duplicate work.
- Confirm whether the SOC2 work blocks can be isolated to just the automation tests or will it impact human review too.

I’m looping priyom and jonas to coordinate the sandbox and support coverage; Marissa on commercial fallback (credits/escrow).

I will provision the quick-run harness and draft the decision ladder doc; sharing by EOD today for your review.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai

Jordan / team — quick operational note from our side on the sandbox approach:

We can provision the async sandbox (mirror of hosted eval config) within 24 hours. Scope and constraints:
- 3 concurrent sessions, 50k token cap total, KV-cache disabled for exactness of evals
- Support SLA for the bucket: triage engineer online 09:00-18:00 PT next 10 business days
- We’ll include a prebuilt scoring script (python) that outputs pass/fail + explanation per test case

Risk grid (quick) — if you pick option 1, residual risks we will track in the slippage log:
- Reviewer turnaround (human review) — likelihood: medium, impact: high — mitigation: submit sample outputs that we pre-score
- Env mismatch (local vs hosted) — likelihood: low, impact: medium — mitigation: config snapshot included in runbook
- Data sensitivity (test vectors) — likelihood: low, impact: high — mitigation: redaction guide and ephemeral storage

If Acme prefers option 2 (hosted extension), we need a PO or credit approval and an ops activation window. Option 3 (decision ladder) requires a sign-off by legal on the suggested escrow language — tagging Marissa for that.

Deliverables we will post by EOD: async_runbook.md, scoring_script.py, and a short acceptance rubric.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — option 1 looks workable. Responses to your asks:
- The two blocked test cases are: (1) high-throughput batch scoring with PHI-masked records (needs config parity), and (2) long-sequence context (>8k tokens) for a chained evaluation. The reviewers can feed synthetic vectors but they prefer the same tokenization/kv behaviour as production.
- SOC2 work: primary blocker is human reviewer bandwidth — they can still accept async submissions but need the pre-scoring to be reliable.

We can provide synthetic vectors for the PHI cases if you confirm redaction and ephemeral storage. I created a short procurement note authorizing a 10-day extension if needed — attaching here. If you can get the sandbox and scoring script by EOD today we’ll run the harness and aim for a verdict next Thursday.

Jordan

Jordan / Elena / team — final status update and escalation note for procurement/legal:

Status: sandbox provisioned (async eval) and scoring script posted. We accepted Acme synthetic vectors with redaction guidance and ephemeral storage per the attached runbook. Timeline: Acme submits by Tue 2027-06-22 11:59 PT; Redwood will return scored results and a triage summary within 24 hours of each submission.

Contingency grid (decision ladder summary):
- Green: two test cases pass -> maintain current close date (no change)
- Amber: one test case fails or reviewer questions remain -> execute 10-day hosted extension (Procurement PO accepted) and Redwood provides two-day response SLA on escalations
- Red: both fail or legal blocks -> formal 14-day re-baseline; Redwood will place price/terms escrow for 30 days (no price change) once legal signs the addendum

Action items (owner / due):
- Acme: submit synthetic vectors and identify expected failure modes (Jordan) / Due: 2027-06-22 11:59 PT
- Redwood: final runbook + scoring script published to shared Drive (Priyom) / Done: 2027-06-18
- Legal: review escrow addendum and DocuSign link (Marissa / Elena) / Due: 2027-06-21

We’ll track the slippage_risk_log as the single source-of-truth and update the MAP export with any gating changes. Looping Marissa for the commercial addendum; Elena for legal sign-off.

— Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
